explanation: The campaign of 1580 was launched from the position the fort at Anzele had held the year before. The article for the campaign says so in its own first paragraph of background. “Cuanza River Campaign”, at revision 1370614389, opens its § Background: “Previously, Paulo Dias de Novais had won a siege in Anzele led by the Ngola forces, consisting of 12,000 men. After the siege, the Ngola warriors sought to make peace with the governor, which he declined, as he already planned to attack them again with a larger force, with the support of the king of Congo.” The second article, “Siege of Anzele” at revision 1370738927, gives the same relation from the other end. It calls the siege “the first military action of the Angolan Wars, which would then continue for over a century”, and dates the Ndongo attack to 1579, before the expedition of May 1580. This edge is typed `precondition-of`. The article credits the governor's own plan for putting the fleet on the river. The siege kept the governor in Angola, which let him make that plan. The confidence is `probable`: rule 22 keeps an edge carried by Wikipedia records below `consensus`, and the chain is the article's own narration rather than a historian's stated judgement.
